checked.found: UNESCO and other sources date Roman exploitation to the 1st century AD (second half in some); 25 BCE is the Augustan conquest of the region, not a sourced start of mining. Sources split; -25 is not confirmed.
Silver at Kutna Hora tied to Wenceslaus II and the Prague groschen (minting from 1300); only a coin-dealer listing gives 1298 for the discovery, and mining near Sedlec began earlier (c. 1260s).
Silver strike 1516 founded Joachimsthal; thaler coins led to the word dollar (one mirror says 1512, most say 1516).
Silver discovered at Zacatecas in 1546.
Gold found in Minas Gerais in 1693, start of the Brazilian gold rush.
Official discovery year is usually given as 1729 (notice to Europe); GIA says uncertain between 1710 and 1730; 1725 appears only in older references.
Gold-bearing quartz found by Erofey Markov at Berezovsk in 1745, first Russian gold.
Conrad Reed found the 17-lb nugget in 1799; used as a doorstop until a jeweller identified it.
Georgia Gold Rush began 1829, first major US rush.
Eureka Diamond found 1867 near Hopetown by children; first South African diamond.
Diamonds found at Colesberg Kopje in 1871, which became the Big Hole.
Ed Schieffelin struck silver in 1877 despite warnings he would find only his tombstone.
Gold reef found 1886; Johannesburg founded.
Arthur Bayley found gold at Coolgardie in 1892.
Gold found at Nome 1899; beach sand rush in 1900.
Found January 1905 by surface manager Frederick Wells; largest gem-quality rough diamond.
Railway worker Zacharias Lewala found a diamond near Luderitz in 1908.
Mir pipe found in 1955 by a Soviet team.
Carlin gold discovery 1961 (microscopic gold).
Orapa pipe found 1967 by De Beers geologists.
Gold found at Serra Pelada in 1980.
Argyle began operations in 1983; main source of pink diamonds.
Fipke and Blusson's Lac de Gras find announced Nov 1991 (Point Lake structure identified 1990).
Found at Karowe mine, Botswana, November 2015; largest gem-quality rough in over a century.
